title: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A rich, slow-simmered meat sauce of beef, pork, tomato, milk and a splash of wine, tossed with spaghetti and Parmesan.

image.alt: A plate of spaghetti topped with meaty bolognese sauce

ingredients.scaleNote: Use a big pot of water whatever the batch size.
It seasons the pasta water, which stays the same amount.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until very soft and lightly golden, {time 10 min}.
Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the beef, pork and salt and cook, breaking up the meat, until it loses its pink color, {time 6-8 min}. Stir in the tomato paste for {time 1 min}.
Pour in the wine and simmer until it evaporates, {time 3 min}. Add the milk and simmer until it’s mostly absorbed, {time 5 min}. The milk makes the meat tender.
Stir in the tomatoes and nutmeg, bring to a bare simmer and cook uncovered, stirring now and then, for {time 1 hr 30 min}. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick before then.
Near the end, bring the water and pasta salt to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente. Save {qty 1/2 cup fixed} of the water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with about two-thirds of the sauce and a splash of pasta water until coated. Serve topped with the rest of the sauce and Parmesan.

notes: The sauce keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months, so it’s worth making a double batch.
A long, gentle simmer is what makes it rich and velvety.
